All figures are arithmetic on public numbers, never achievable value; unknown buckets: 2 periods. Duration-awareness alone removed 44.8 percent of what physics permitted - the first quantified measure of what GC0166 data adds to counterfactual credibility.

arguments.value: CORRECTION of fnd-bess-001-fragility (which remains on the record as published): the GBP 1,263,589 point-in-time figure was a pooled NET difference concealing revisions in both directions. Period-level decomposition: final-vintage MDO/MDB supported GBP 4,689,718 of opportunity not publicly supportable at the decision cutoff (989 unit-direction-periods) AND removed GBP 3,426,133 that the contemporaneous public envelope had supported (1,991 unit-direction-periods); net GBP 1,263,584 (the GBP 5 residue is two unknown-at-R3p periods). A hindsight benchmark does not merely know more - it reconstructs a materially different feasible state from the one publicly observable at decision time, in either direction. All other figures of the original finding are unchanged and reconfirmed (rung totals byte-identical on re-run); the timeliness claim is corrected to: July 2026 is the first full month for which the new public MDO/MDB data exists. Figures are arithmetic on public numbers, never achievable value.

arguments.value: PARTLY CONFIRMED, with the observability boundary precisely mapped. The frozen rule selected constraint group SSE-SP, 2026-05-18..31 (right-censored by the window): 8,259 repeat-curtailment cycles consistent with RRT, 69,869 MWh storage bid-down. The observable sequence reconstructs at scale (excerpt day 2026-05-20: 1,060 cycles; focus unit E_DOLLB-1: 21 cycles, 88 distinct acceptances in one day, repeatedly instructed from scheduled export through zero to around -99 MW import, NONE SO-flagged in the public record). Published money accounts to Elexon's own indicative figures (episode dates, GB-wide scope: storage bids -6,736,338 GBP, storage offers +9,152,108, non-storage offers +78,392,272; SSE-SP published outturn constraint cost 11,510,565 GBP). Two links are NOT publicly observable and are the finding: (1) the intraday re-sale that turns repetition into re-trading; (2) the unit-to-constraint-group mapping that would localise money to the boundary. No figure is a cost of RRT; concurrency is observed, substitution never asserted.

arguments.value: CORRECTION AND STRENGTHENING of fnd-003-episode-reconstructed (which remains on the record as published). (1) Attribution: the frozen selection rule scores an episode by counting repeat-curtailment cycles across the entire declared GB storage universe over the episode dates; no constraint-group filter was declared and none is publicly implementable - the missing unit-to-group mapping the original finding itself identified. The 8,259 cycles and 69,869 MWh are GB-wide storage activity concurrent with the SSE-SP episode dates and must not be presented as activity behind SSE-SP. (2) Methodology alignment, from the pinned Ofgem RRT policy paper (June 2026, art-003-ofgem-rrt-paper): NESO estimates the balancing cost impact of RRT from storage at approximately GBP 99m in FY 2025/26 (12-hour search window), up from approximately GBP 64m in FY 2024/25, with pumped storage around 80 percent of the two-year total; the methodology counts only settlement periods with a positive FPN, a SYSTEM-FLAGGED bid acceptance, and a subsequent net-upward PN revision within a 3/6/12-hour horizon - computed from timestamped PN revision history that is not public (only final PN vintages are). (3) Descriptive tally over the episode dates (evidence: so-flag-tally.json): 90,020 distinct storage-unit acceptances GB-wide, of which 2,904 (3.2 percent) are SO-flagged; focus unit E_DOLLB-1 recorded 1,492 acceptances with zero SO-flagged, so its 21 excerpt-day cycles cannot be presented as a demonstrated constraint-driven RRT example. Consequence: the repeat-curtailment score is a concurrence signature, not NESO's RRT count, and the public record cannot reproduce NESO's RRT diagnosis - the missing inputs are point-in-time PN revision history and authoritative constraint attribution.
